newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on commercials, Brazil tax talk.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on commercials, Brazil tax talk.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on commercial demand and rumour Brazil would impose an export tax on soybeans, traders said.

"Brazil was more of a factor as the day wore on prompting commission demand in futures and call options, UGG bought, (ADM unit) Benson Quinn bought 500 November, Japan bought May and July, Cargill sold May and July all day," a trader said. May WCE futures crush profit margin rose to -14.35 Friday from -14.69 Thursday. About 700 May-July spread at $0.90, May-Nov $53.50. Volume was 7,977 lots with 1,060 hedges.
Japan bought 4,000-5,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.

May canola rose $6.60 to $431.50, July up $6.40 to $431.70 and November rose $5.20 to $377.20. May flax ended unchanged at $359 on commercial demand met by hedges. July-Nov spread at $34. Volume was 140 lots, 40 hedges. Oats did not trade.

May feed wheat rose $3.20 to $174 as commission buy stops were triggered at $173 and Alberta Wheat Pool sold, July up $2.10 to $171. Midland-Walwyn bought 250 May-July at $3, Mar-May spread at $10, traders said. Volume was 1,600 lots.
May western barley rose $2 to $145.20 on commercial buying after commission buy stops were hit at $146 and AWP sold at $145, Louis Dreyfus bought July up $1.70 to $142.60, traders.
(All values in Canadian dollars, except feed peas)
